newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Deutsche sees 25 pct Lithuania litas devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche sees 25 pct Lithuania litas devaluation.

text.p: Lithuania's currency, the litas, is likely to undergo a devaluation of 25 percent as it changes its monetary policy to end the present currency board system, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Thursday.

The central bank plans gradually to end the currency board system of fixing the litas at four to one dollar. It says it will do it in three stages, keeping the present fixed rate until at least 1999. It has dismissed any talk of a devaluation.
But Deutsche said in a report that the three-stage approach made little sense as keeping a fixed exchange rate without the backing of a currency board was "inviting trouble".
It said that the most likely alternative to the present currency board regime was a flexible, pre-announced crawling peg to a basket of currencies, similar to Hungary and Poland.
It said this would most likely be accompanied by a one-time devaluation to correct for a 25 percent real appreciation of the currency during 1995/96 and to reverse a growing trade deficit.
"Therefore, our most likely scenario is a switch of the exchange rate in the next few weeks, probably to a new parity of five litas for one U.S. dollar," the report said.
It said that if there was a severe speculative attack, there was a possibility of "overshooting" with a larger depreciation before a crawling peg could be established.

The central bank has said that the three stages would involve a gradual return of the bank's powers to influence monetary policy, almost non-existent under a currency board, by starting open money market operations.

The second stage would involve ending the currency board no earlier than 1998. The third stage involves changing the litas peg after 1999 to either a peg to the dollar and the planned European currency, the euro, or the euro alone.
The central bank and the government have repeatedly said their plans do not include any devaluation.
